result.title: Two Routes to Interoceptive Prioritisation: Dissociating Likelihood Precision and Preference Reweighting in Active Inference
result.comment: Accepted at IWAI 2026, forthcoming in the Springer proceedings. 17 pages: the 13-page camera-ready paper, reproduced without alteration apart from one typographical fix, followed by 4 pages of supplementary material. Code: https://github.com/sgrimbly/interoceptive-prioritisation-iwai2026-snapshot
result.summary: An embodied agent must prioritise among competing bodily needs. In active inference, it can respond to an urgent need by increasing the precision of information about that need or by increasing its preference for outcomes that relieve it. We compare these two interventions, separately and together, in a foraging gridworld with three lethal needs, and ask how each changes survival, perception and the body model the agent learns. Precision sharpens interoceptive posteriors and improves survival. Preference reweighting keeps bodily states further from their lethal boundaries and changes the states from which the agent learns, so its learned model covers fewer need levels, with lower quality across all levels but slightly higher quality on the levels it visits. An experiment on 72 further layouts does not establish the predicted preference benefit on difficult layouts, but both interventions improve average survival there and their interaction is positive. Survival alone therefore gives an incomplete account of how a model prioritises needs and learns about its body.

AI.brief_summary: 在含三种致命需求的多智能体觅食网格世界中，比较 active inference 下两种优先化干预——提高内感受似然的精度、以及重塑对缓解结果的偏好——单独与联合使用时对生存、感知及所学身体模型的影响，并指出仅用生存率不足以刻画模型如何优先化需求。
AI.relevance_reason: 精度加权与偏好重加权可视为「证据 vs 目标」两种优先化机制，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据筛选与 latent 状态加权提供概念线索；论文还显示干预会改变智能体学习所依据的状态分布，可供核查训练监督与贡献分配问题，但属远领域推测。
